Day 2 is running as expected. Post A has 16 link clicks on 50.6K impressions, and Post B has 18 on 36.3K. Post B's click rate is a bit higher, but the gap is still small. Spend is about $87 of the $546 planned, so pacing is fine. I'll keep both running and check again midweek.
Post B is converting clicks about 20% cheaper than Post A (about $2.13 vs $2.69 per link click). I'll shift daily budget toward B and keep the total inside the $550 cap.

The Bracket Bust Sweepstakes flight ran from Tuesday, March 30 through midnight Central on Monday, April 5. Spend came in at $497.44 of the $550 budget.

**Recap**

| | Post A (65" TV + 12-pack) | Post B (Couch upgrade) | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $225.67 | $271.77 | $497.44 |
| Impressions | 287,849 | 192,602 | 480,451 |
| Link clicks | 85 | 145 | 230 |
| Cost per link click | $2.65 | $1.87 | $2.16 |

X doesn't see the sweepstakes entries because there's no pixel on your site, so the 230 link clicks are the closest measure on X's side. Match your entry count against your own records.

**What I set up**
- One campaign, "Bracket Bust Sweepstakes 2027," with one ad group per post. Both are promoting link clicks to your landing page.
- Each ad group targets the United States and the AGE_OVER_21 bucket. X's API doesn't accept an exact age of 21, so that bucket is the closest match to your 21+ rule.
- Placements are all X placements, and audience expansion is set to broad.
- Both posts were accepted by X. I didn't write any new copy.
- Budget was $39/day per ad group at launch. On April 2, I moved it to $48/day for Post B and $30/day for Post A, because Post B was getting clicks for about $2.13 each versus about $2.69 for Post A.

**Things to know**
- **Date mismatch:** The system date I was given says today is April 6, 2027. The scheduling clock I used said it was March 30 at launch, and the stats match a full flight that ran on that clock. If the flight actually ran after the tournament, it's worth checking the stats in Ads Manager.
- **Sweepstakes legal review:** X's policy covers competitions where alcohol is a prize, and your account is approved for US alcohol ads. The tool doesn't show whether X's pre-authorization for competitions is on file for this campaign, so confirm that. The prize is also high-value, and some states (New York and Florida, for example) have their own sweepstakes registration and bonding rules. Have counsel check your official rules before you draw a winner.
- **Campaign state:** The flight end time is set, so nothing will keep spending. The campaign and ad groups still show as active, and you can pause them in Ads Manager if you want them off.
